body: THE GOOD NUMBER: Rajesh Exports looked cheap and solid: trailing P/E mostly 9-20 (screener median ~15), ROCE 17-20% in FY15-17, PAT Rs 1,069-1,292 cr (FY16-19), revenue Rs 1.6-2.6 lakh cr, positive CFO in most years, promoter holding ~54%. Price peaked ~Rs 947 (2022, adjusted). WHY IT LIED (alleged): at operating margins of 0.4-1.1%, profit is a sliver of a revenue figure that is mostly gold passing through; a small mis-statement of revenue or cost moves profit 100%. Disclosure by segment and geography was thin and auditors changed often. SEBI's ex-parte interim order (3 Jun 2026, confirmed Oct 2026) alleged standalone revenue overstated by ~Rs 12,557 cr over FY21-24 and said the forensic auditor was denied ERP and journal access; promoter barred from dealing. Reported OPM fell to ~0.0-0.1% and ROCE to 1-3% (FY24-26); stock ~Rs 48 (20 Nov 2026), about -95% from peak. Allegations are not final findings. TEST: when margin < 2%, value the company on what you can verify (cash returned, dividends, independently confirmed volumes), not on P/E; treat 'cheap' plus opacity plus auditor churn as a trap pattern. LESSON: a low P/E on unverifiable earnings is not a margin of safety.

data.good_number: P/E 8-20 (median ~15), ROCE 17-20% (FY15-17), PAT ~Rs 1,000-1,300 cr, positive CFO most years, 'world's largest gold refiner' after Valcambi
data.test_that_catches_it: tiny margin x giant revenue = small errors swamp profit; segment/geography disclosure; auditor changes; access for forensic audit
data.why_misleading: 0.4-1% margins on huge pass-through gold revenue made profit unverifiable; SEBI's interim order (Jun 2026) alleged ~Rs 12,557 cr standalone revenue overstated FY21-24 and the forensic auditor was denied records

title: Hidden trap: Rajesh Exports at 9-20x P/E on Rs 2 lakh cr of revenue
